transcript:
[doctor] Hi John, how are you doing today?

[patient] Hi doctor, I’m doing okay. How are you?

[doctor] I’m good, thank you. I see that you’ve come in today for fatigue, decreased libido, and difficulty concentrating. Can you tell me a little more about these symptoms?

[patient] Sure, I’ve been feeling really tired all the time for the past six months. It doesn't seem to get better no matter what I do. Also, my sex drive has gone down, and I'm having a hard time focusing at work. I’m an accountant, so concentrating is really important for my job.

[doctor] Hmm, that sounds challenging. Have you noticed any other symptoms or changes in your health?

[patient] Not really, just those main issues. I’ve tried changing my diet and getting more sleep, but nothing seems to help.

[doctor] I see. Let’s go over some details about your general health. Are you experiencing any other issues, like weight gain or loss, or any other discomfort?

[patient] No, my weight has been pretty stable. I haven't noticed any other discomfort either.

[doctor] Okay, and how about your concentration? Is it affecting your ability to complete tasks at work?

[patient] Yes, it’s been really hard to stay focused, and it’s impacting my work performance. I feel like I’m always in a fog.

[doctor] Alright, and about your libido, can you tell me more about how it has changed?

[patient] It’s just not there anymore. My interest in sex has really decreased, and it's affecting my relationship with my partner.

[doctor] Got it. Have you had any previous issues with your health, particularly related to your hormones or any chronic conditions?

[patient] No, nothing like that. I’ve generally been pretty healthy.

[doctor] Okay, and you mentioned trying lifestyle changes. Can you tell me more about what you've tried?

[patient] I’ve tried eating healthier, cutting out junk food, and getting more sleep, but nothing seems to make a difference.

[doctor] Alright, let’s take a look at your vital signs and do a quick physical exam. Your blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, heart rate is 72 bpm, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, and your temperature is 98.6°F. Your BMI is 27.5 kg/m². On physical examination, you appear well-nourished and well-developed. Your cardiovascular exam is normal, and there are no murmurs, rubs, or gallops. Genitourinary exam shows normal genitalia but with smaller testicular volume bilaterally. Neurological exam is also normal with no focal deficits. 

[patient] Okay, that sounds good. What does all that mean?

[doctor] Well, your vital signs are within a reasonable range, though your blood pressure is slightly elevated. Your physical exam is mostly normal, except for the smaller testicular volume which could be related to your symptoms of fatigue, decreased libido, and difficulty concentrating.

[patient] I see. What do you think could be causing these symptoms?

[doctor] Based on your symptoms and physical findings, it’s possible that you might have testicular hypofunction, which means your testes might not be producing enough hormones, particularly testosterone.

[patient] Oh, I see. What can be done about that?

[doctor] We’ve ordered some blood tests to check your hormone levels, including Total Testosterone, Free Testosterone, LH, FSH, and Prolactin. Once we get those results back, we’ll have a better idea. In the meantime, I’m going to start you on Hormone Replacement Therapy with Testosterone Cypionate 100 mg/mL via intramuscular injection every 2 weeks.

[patient] Alright, how long will I need to be on this treatment?

[doctor] The duration will depend on how you respond to the therapy. We’ll monitor your hormone levels and symptoms closely. I’d like you to follow up in one month to assess how you’re doing and to check your hormone levels again.

[patient] Okay, that sounds reasonable. 

[doctor] Additionally, I’m referring you to an endocrinologist, Dr. Jane Smith, for further evaluation and long-term management of your condition.

[patient] Okay, I’ll make sure to see Dr. Smith.

[doctor] Great. I also want to emphasize the importance of lifestyle modifications. Continue to make healthier dietary choices, reduce processed food intake, and aim for at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week.

[patient] I’ll do my best with that.

[doctor] Excellent. It’s also crucial to adhere to the prescribed medication regimen and follow-up appointments. There can be potential side effects, and we need to monitor your therapy closely.

[patient] Understood. What kind of side effects should I be aware of?

[doctor] Some possible side effects include mood changes, acne, and fluid retention. We’ll discuss these in more detail during your follow-up.

[patient] Alright, I’ll keep an eye out for those.

[doctor] Also, remember to continue your current medications for hypertension and high cholesterol: lisinopril 20 mg daily and atorvastatin 10 mg daily.

[patient] Yes, I’ve been taking those regularly.

[doctor] Good to hear. Do you have any other questions or concerns?

[patient] Not at the moment. Thank you for your help, doctor.

[doctor] You’re welcome, John. I’m hopeful that with the right treatment and lifestyle changes, you’ll start to see improvements soon. Remember to schedule your follow-up appointment and contact me if you have any issues before then.

[patient] Will do. Thanks again.

[doctor] Take care, John. See you in a month.
